cards.title: Perspective (1, 2 and 3-point)
cards.body: The horizon line is always at the viewer's eye level. One-point: you face a flat side; depth lines meet at one vanishing point (roads, corridors). Two-point: you face a corner; two vanishing points sit on the horizon, verticals stay vertical. Three-point: looking up or down; verticals also converge. Things get smaller and closer together with distance.

cards.title: Foreshortening
cards.body: When an object points towards or away from you, its length looks compressed and the near end looks bigger. An arm pointing at you becomes overlapping circles, not a long tube. Use overlap, size change and stronger detail on the near end. Measure what you see, not what you know the length to be.

cards.title: Light & shade
cards.body: Highlight: the brightest spot, facing the light. Form shadow: the darker side of the object, turned away from the light. Cast shadow: the shadow the object throws onto other surfaces, falling away from the light. Reflected light: a faint glow on the shadow side. Low light → long shadows; overhead light → short shadows. Keep one light direction throughout.

cards.title: Human figure proportion
cards.body: An adult is about 7–8 heads tall. Hips are at about half the height; elbows at the waist; fingertips at mid-thigh; knees about a quarter of the way up from the feet. Shoulders are about 2–3 head-widths wide. Children have larger heads in proportion (about 4–6 heads tall). Start with the line of action, then a stick figure, then simple volumes.

cards.title: Texture rendering
cards.body: Texture is shown by the kind of marks you make. Wood: long wavy lines and knots. Stone: dots, speckles and cracks. Metal: sharp contrast and crisp highlights. Glass: reflections and see-through edges. Fabric: soft folds radiating from points of tension. Cane and jute: weave patterns. Match the mark to the material, and keep texture lighter in the light.

cards.title: Line quality
cards.body: Confident lines are drawn in one stroke from the shoulder, not scratched. Vary weight: thicker for near edges, shadow sides and overlaps; thinner for far edges and light sides. Contour lines describe form; construction lines stay light. Clean line quality makes even simple drawings look professional.
